'''Jonathan Karl Pritchard''' is an English-born professor of genetics at Stanford University, best known for his development of the STRUCTURE algorithm for studying population structure and his work on human genetic variation and evolution.<ref name=":0">Pritchard Lab website:  http://pritchardlab.stanford.edu</ref>  His research interests lie in the study of [[human evolution]], in particular in understanding the association between genetic variation among human individuals and human traits.<ref name=googlescholar>{{GoogleScholar|iopnWAMAAAAJ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal

==Education==
Pritchard's family moved to the US when he was a teenager. He studied [[biology]] and [[mathematics]] at [[Pennsylvania State University]], and then went on to graduate studies in biology at [[Stanford University]] under the supervision of Marc Feldman, finishing in 1998.<ref name="hhmi"/>

==Career==
Pritchard conducted [[postdoctoral research]] with [[Peter Donnelly]] at the University of Oxford. It was there that he developed STRUCTURE, a widely used computer program for determining [[population stratification|population structure]] and estimating individual [[Genetic admixture|admixture]].<ref name="structure" /> In 2001, he moved to the [[University of Chicago]]. He was promoted from Assistant Professor to Full Professor in 2006. He stayed there until moving to Stanford in 2013.<ref name=":0" />  He was awarded a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] (HHMI) investigator position in 2008.<ref name="hhmi">[http://www.hhmi.org/news/pritchard_bio.html Jonathan K. Pritchard, Ph.D.], Bios of the 2008 New HHMI Investigators, HHMI, retrieved 2011-07-24.</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Pritchard was a recipient of the 2013 [[Edward Novitski Prize]] from the [[Genetics Society of America]] and the 2002 [[Mitchell Prize]] from the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]].

==Personal life==
Pritchard ran track and cross country for [[Pennsylvania State University]] from 1989 to 1994. In part because of his running experience, he appeared in the 1998 movie [[Without Limits]] portraying [[David Bedford (athlete)|David Bedford]], an English distance runner who participated in the 1972 Munich Olympics.
